evidence.title: JSON Schema Validation
evidence.author: A. Wright, H. Andrews, B. Hutton (editors)
limitations: Internet-Draft/work in progress, not an RFC
Format assertions vary by vocabulary and implementation

evidence.title: PROV-Overview
evidence.author: Paul Groth and Luc Moreau (editors)
limitations: Same standards family as E-003; not independent empirical corroboration

evidence.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
evidence.author: Luc Moreau and Paolo Missier (editors)
limitations: A provenance record is itself an artifact needing assessment

claims.text: JSON Schema checks declared constraints and can express defined semantic formats; it is too broad to say it cannot check any semantic property.
claims.uncertainty: Assertion behavior depends on vocabulary/implementation; not arbitrary citation entailment

claims.text: PROV describes provenance as information used to assess quality and trustworthiness.
claims.uncertainty: A stated purpose is not measured empirical accuracy

claims.text: PROV-DM describes provenance of provenance, including responsibility and generation context.
claims.uncertainty: The cited overview is informative; provenance still needs assessment

claims.text: RAMP should distinguish formal/reference checks from a separate judgment that a cited passage supports a research claim.
claims.reasoning: Declared constraints and provenance context make records inspectable; neither supplies a general entailment test for an arbitrary research claim.
claims.uncertainty: Design inference from three related technical sources; no general agent-performance result
